purpose: Review a study cited by the 2023 Mountain Province rice-field paper, retaining it as a separate aquaculture sample and preventing cultured-pond evidence from being represented as river/lake occurrence.

study.title: Length-weight relationship and condition factor of male and female Japanese weather loach (Misgurnus anguillicaudatus) grown in ponds in Bauko, Mountain Province, Philippines
study.citation: Reyes, A. T., Juan, A. G. M., Gamurot, Z. T., Aguilar, A. S., Watiwat, W. D. R., Dizon, E. L., Suva, C. G. C., Cayco, C. S., Valenzuela, Z. M., Martin, D. V., Samonte, L. J. M., & Dalagan, S. T. (2019). International Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Studies, 7(4), 158-160.
methodsAsReported: The paper reports hand-collecting 78 loaches from two fish ponds in Bauko, Mountain Province.
The samples were separated by sex using pectoral-fin and abdomen characteristics, then measured for length and weight.
The paper does not name the ponds or give their coordinates, collection dates, pond-level sample breakdown, species-identification procedure, specimen accession numbers, or repository.

evidenceLimits: The authors label the samples Misgurnus anguillicaudatus, but the paper describes sex sorting rather than a species-identification procedure and provides no independently checkable voucher or accession record.
These are fish-pond samples explicitly described as grown in ponds; they do not establish a wild population, river or lake occurrence, or site-level distribution in Bauko.
No exact sampling date or pond-specific result is provided, so the study cannot be assigned to a current season or particular waterbody polygon.
The abstract and discussion reverse the male/female mean-length and mean-weight labels relative to Table 1; do not import sex-specific metrics without author clarification.

The paper's introductory feed list (insect larvae, snails, worms, ostracods, cladocerans, fish eggs, algae and detritus) is attributed to a cited background source, not measured in these pond samples. It is not local diet evidence and is not an app-ready diet claim.

The introductory statement that the loach was introduced to the Philippines before World War II is not substantiated by field evidence in this study and should not be treated as a verified introduction date.

relationshipTo2023Study.assessment: The 2023 paper cites this 2019 pond-culture study as prior work. It reports a different sample scope (two ponds versus three rice-field/terrace stations) and no shared specimens, collection dates, pond-to-ricefield crosswalk, or voucher link. Keep the two sources separate.

reuseReview.decision: The reviewed publisher-hosted PDF carries a 2019 copyright line but no item-specific Creative Commons or data license was verified. Retain citation and concise research notes only; do not redistribute the PDF, tables, or derived app data without permission.

nextAction: The introductory diet list was traced to Milton et al. (2018), a secondary review. A separate Idaho stomach-content paper provides foreign-population evidence only; neither source establishes local Philippine diet. For future diet features, seek native-range and Philippine field studies tied to identified specimens, waterbody and season. Keep this distinct from the two-pond aquaculture sample and wild occurrences.

sources.supports: The 2019 paper title, authors, receipt/acceptance dates, two-pond Bauko sampling context, 78 hand-collected loaches and reported sex counts.
